pr_title: logind: Properly unescape names of lingering users
pr_body:
Filenames to store user linger requests are created with C-escaping. When we enumerate the files to acquire ligering users we use the filenames verbatim. In the casue C-escaping is not an identity map (such as "DOMAIN\User"), we won't be able to start user instances of such mangled users.

Unescape filenames when we treat them as usernames again.

Fixes: #25448
pr_comments: looks pretty good, but see my comment: we prefer if log messages are precise and we say clearly that we ignore things.

issue_context.title: issues with linger and username containing \ character
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

252

### Used distribution

debian testing - package  252.1-1 

### Linux kernel version used

6.0.0-4-amd64

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

_No response_

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

When doing 

loginctl enable-linger DOMAIN\\user

Observations:
- notice two backslashes as it is executed from the shell command line
- the command generates '/var/lib/systemd/linger/DOMAIN\\user'  with two back slashes
- I would be expecting that the file generated were '/var/lib/systemd/linger/DOMAIN\user' (only one back slash, as the user name has only one backslash)
- Session processes are started for the user without issue
- loginctl show-user reports linger as active

- PROBLEM: after a reboot the user session is not started, and loginctl show-user DOMAIN\user reports linger disabled

- Even if creating a file such as  '/var/lib/systemd/linger/DOMAIN\user'  manually, the session processes are not started after a reboot

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

_No response_

_No response_

_No response_
comments:
Thanks for the report @flucas1.

Possible workaroud: `touch` the file manually but the filename must have double backslash (i.e. `Domain\\User`). `systemd-logind` should pick it up after reboot.

Proposed proper fix in #25529.
